library_preparation_preflight.agent_guidance: Write tests against the core abstraction types (io.micronaut.cache.SyncCache, AsyncCache, CacheManager) and the @Cacheable/@CachePut/@CacheInvalidate annotations rather than against Caffeine-specific APIs — Caffeine is only present to supply a working CacheManager bean. Scope user-code-filter.json / allowed-packages to io.micronaut.cache core classes and avoid pulling io.micronaut.cache.caffeine.** into this library's shipped metadata, since that package is already owned and covered by the sibling micronaut-cache-caffeine metadata. No extra environment variables or system properties are expected; Micronaut auto-configures the CacheManager from the single backend on the classpath.
risks: If Gradle/Native Image verification shows micronaut-cache-core actually resolves a usable CacheManager without any backend (e.g. a built-in no-op/local default), the added caffeine dependency would be unnecessary — local verification is authoritative over this desk review.
Loose package filtering could cause Caffeine-specific classes to leak into micronaut-cache-core's shipped metadata instead of staying confined to the sibling micronaut-cache-caffeine artifact.
